objective: Program allocation v2 (P4): choose a walk-forward, forecast-free allocation of the paper sleeves that beats the ETF pilot P0 (0.642 S3 + 0.358 C2) at the same volatility, or else the tightest single-sleeve risk-share cap whose recent Sharpe cost is within 0.10 and that helps in stress; size it per capital tier and account type under the ~30% drawdown budget, minimum sleeve capital and Alpaca margin rules, and report DSR-deflated drawdown quantiles.

sources.core_claim: Maillard, Roncalli and Teiletche (Journal of Portfolio Management 36(4), 2010): the equally-weighted risk contribution (ERC) portfolio equalises Euler risk contributions; its volatility lies between the minimum-variance and the 1/N portfolios; empirical applications confirm the ranking; ERC is presented as a trade-off in absolute risk, risk budgeting and diversification.
sources.project_applicability: Defines the ERC rule and the capped risk-budget rule (CAP2) via the same risk-budgeting problem; no expected-return input.
sources.reflection: Asset-class and equity-index illustrations; says nothing about combining levered ETF momentum sleeves or about Sharpe gains.

sources.core_claim: DeMiguel, Garlappi and Uppal (RFS 22(5), 2009), abstract: of 14 optimised models across seven datasets none is consistently better than 1/N in Sharpe ratio, certainty-equivalent return or turnover; the estimation window needed for sample mean-variance to beat 1/N is about 3000 months for 25 assets.
sources.project_applicability: No rule in this contract estimates expected returns from data; weights come from trailing covariance only (CAP2, ERC, IV) or are static (P0, 1/N report-only).
sources.reflection: Abstract only (full text paywalled; LBS repository has no full text). Asset universes are equity portfolios, not strategy sleeves.

sources.core_claim: Palomar, Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Application (Cambridge 2025), ch. 11: risk parity allocates risk rather than dollars; 1/N diversifies capital but one asset can dominate risk; convex formulations (Spinu) solve the risk-budgeting problem; cites Chaves-Hsu-Li-Shakernia 2011 (risk parity beats min-variance and mean-variance but not consistently 1/N).
sources.project_applicability: Solver choice (convex risk-budgeting formulation) and the 1/N report-only benchmark.
sources.reflection: Academic textbook (not a journal paper); Textbook; illustrations on equities; Chaves et al. 2011 cited, not read in full.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca: 50% initial margin (Reg T); overnight maintenance 30% for long positions above $6, 50% for 2x and 75% for 3x leveraged ETFs; debit interest 6.50%/yr non-elite charged on overnight debit /360; a single security above 70% of equity market value with a margin balance >= $100,000 gets 50% maintenance.
sources.project_applicability: Margin-account feasibility filter (S3 0.75, other ETF sleeves 0.30), debit 0.065*365/360 per year, gross <= 2.0.
sources.reflection: Page content as fetched 2026-10-05; Alpaca may change rates; live accounts may differ from paper.

sources.core_claim: FINRA Regulatory Notice 09-53 (effective 2009-12-01): maintenance margin for leveraged ETFs rises by the leverage factor (long 25% x leverage, short 30% x leverage, capped at 100%).
sources.project_applicability: Confirms the 0.75 maintenance used for S3's 3x ETFs (T-43 marked it 待核对; now verified).
sources.reflection: Industry minimum; brokers may set higher house requirements.

sources.core_claim: Bailey and Lopez de Prado (JPM 40(5), 2014): the Deflated Sharpe Ratio corrects for selection bias under multiple testing and for non-normal returns; the benchmark SR0 is the expected maximum Sharpe of N independent trials.
sources.project_applicability: Haircut h_i = max(0, SR_i - SR0_i)/SR_i for the deflated-mean drawdown simulation; DSR of the selected deployable with N = 8.
sources.reflection: Needs a trial count; ETF sleeve counts come from T-20261005-31.

sources.core_claim: Magdon-Ismail, Atiya, Pratap and Abu-Mostafa (J. Applied Probability 41, 2004): the expected maximum drawdown of Brownian motion grows logarithmically in time for positive drift, linearly for negative drift and as sqrt(T) for zero drift.
sources.project_applicability: Drawdown quantiles depend on the assumed edge; the contract simulates three edges (deflated recent, stress-window mean, zero).
sources.reflection: Brownian motion; the contract uses a stationary block bootstrap to keep fat tails and volatility clustering.

sources.core_claim: Kaminski and Lo (Journal of Financial Markets 18, 2014): stop-loss rules add value only when returns are not a random walk (momentum or regime switching); under a random walk they reduce expected return.
sources.project_applicability: Drawdown quantiles are reported as halve and stop thresholds in the tail (95%, 99%), not as a tight stop.

sources.core_claim: Roncalli and Weisang (MPRA 44017, 2012): Euler risk contributions hold for assets and factors; asset-level risk budgets can leave factor risk unbalanced (ERC over 7 equity + 3 bond indices puts 70% of risk in equities).
sources.project_applicability: Sleeve risk share = Euler contribution; the account-level semiconductor share is reported because sleeve-level ERC can still concentrate theme risk (S2 and S3 both hold semis).
